D006-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been working nights at the station, and for about 10 months now it feels like I’ve been on this roller coaster I can’t get off. Most of the time I’m either way up or way down, but the “up” has been there almost this whole time.

When I’m up, I’m wired. At work I’ll start cleaning the pumps, then halfway through I’m in the stockroom rearranging shelves, then I’m outside washing windows, all at once. I never finish anything. My mood flips fast—I’ll be laughing, feeling like everything is amazing, then someone looks at me weird and I snap, get really pissed for no reason.

For the last 8 months, I keep seeing people out by the pumps or in the corner of the store who disappear when I look twice. I’m convinced the customers and even the radio are sending me messages, like certain songs or phrases are about me.

There was a stretch a couple months where I wasn’t “up” or “down,” just flat, but the visions and messages kept going. And for about 3 months now, when the energy drops, nothing feels good anymore. I don’t enjoy anything, and sometimes I get these sudden urges to just step into traffic on the highway outside the station.
D006-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h002.question:
It started about ten months ago. I went from feeling on top of the world to snapping at my husband over nothing, sometimes within the same hour. I’d stay up all night pacing, reorganizing my office, writing half-baked article ideas on scraps of paper. I just couldn’t sit still, even in faculty meetings; I’d leave halfway through because I literally couldn’t stay in the chair or follow the conversation for more than a minute.

Around eight months ago, things got…strange. I began to feel things crawling on my skin, like invisible insects running up my arms and legs, even when I could see nothing there. At times, my speech would fall apart—I’d start a sentence about my research and end up stringing unrelated words together so badly my colleagues would stare, confused.

I’m convinced something catastrophic is coming—that the world, or at least our city, is about to be wiped out. That belief sticks even when my mood shifts. There were a couple of weeks where I barely had any of the up-and-down mood swings, but the crawling sensations and the certainty of impending destruction kept going.

For the past three months, everything crashed. I stopped caring about my classes, missed grading deadlines, and a few weeks ago I stockpiled my leftover painkillers and wrote letters to my husband and parents, planning not to wake up. My work and home life have really fallen apart through all of this.
D006-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
